Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our call, attached is a short draft sizing that maps your expected traffic fingerprint to a recommended Dedicated slab and a proposed initial canary. High-level summary up front:

- Baseline workload: interactive summarization + contextual chat (avg payload ~150 tokens/request).
- Target SLOs: p95 generation latency <= 350ms (APIGW-to-first-token), sustained p50 < 120ms.
- Recommended committed slab for initial production: 12x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (reserved).
- First-month canary: 4x GPUs behind a canary routing policy; monitor token-level cost and p95 tail for two weeks.
- Headroom & burst: design for 2.5x peak headroom (based on expected marketing-triggered bursts).

I've attached a quick spreadsheet (saffron-draft-sizing.xlsx) with the token/sec math and a one-pager MAP (Saffron-MAP-v1.docx). Karthik is cc'd and will follow up with a technical breakdown of assumptions (quantization, KV cache hit rates, average tokens per request, concurrency distribution).

Samir — thanks for the detail. Below is the technical breakdown and the assumptions I used. I put the CSV with the per-endpoint rows in saffron-sizing-detailed.csv (attached).

Assumptions (conservative):
- Model variant: 40B dense -> quantized INT8 path (production preference for Saffron). We assume throughput equivalent to ~1.2x performance of baseline open 30B due to kernel selection.
- Average tokens per category (use your distribution): chat 60, summarization 220, long-gen 600.
- Request composition: 60% chat, 30% summarization, 10% long-gen.
- Cache hit rate: 40% KV prefix cache for chat/summarization flows; when hit, avg token generation drops ~35% (less context to regenerate).
- Concurrency target per GPU: measured at ~180 concurrent tokens/sec for the chosen quantized runtime on an A100-80GB-equivalent (p50 latency within 80–120ms for small requests).

Estimated tokens/sec calculation (steady baseline):
- Request rate baseline: 400 req/min = 6.67 req/sec.
- Token/sec baseline = sum(category_share * req/sec * avg_tokens)
  = 0.6*6.67*60 + 0.3*6.67*220 + 0.1*6.67*600
  = 24.0 + 44.0 + 40.0 = ~108 tokens/sec (baseline).

Peak tokens/sec (3,000 req/min = 50 req/sec):
  = 0.6*50*60 + 0.3*50*220 + 0.1*50*600
  = 1,800 + 3,300 + 3,000 = 8,100 tokens/sec (peak).

Effective tokens/sec after cache (40% hit -> 35% token reduction on hits):
- Effective reduction factor = 1 - 0.4*0.35 = 0.86
- Baseline effective tokens/sec = 108 * 0.86 = ~93 t/s
- Peak effective tokens/sec = 8,100 * 0.86 = ~6,966 t/s

GPU mapping (A100-80GB-equivalent):
- Sustained capacity per GPU (conservative): 180 t/s
- Baseline GPUs required = ceil(93 / 180) = 1 GPU (baseline) - but we don't recommend 1 GPU for HA/maintenance reasons.
- Peak GPUs required (no headroom) = ceil(6966 / 180) = 39 GPUs.

Headroom and SLO target mapping:
- To meet p95 <= 350ms during peaks, we recommend baseline headroom factor of 2.5x on top of peak required GPUs to absorb bursty arrival patterns and node-level variance.
- Recommended committed slab sizing = 39 * 2.5 = 97.5 -> round to 96 GPUs (reserved slab).

Practical commercial recommendation (blended reliability + cost tradeoff):
- Option A (conservative enterprise): 96x GPUs reserved (SLA-backed, single-region), with auto-burst to cloud pool for extra peaks. Provides comfortable p95 headroom but is a heavy commit.
- Option B (phased commit, lower initial cost): Start with 12x GPUs reserved + 60x burst capacity on-demand (burst to shared pool). Canary 4x for month 1 to validate workload shape. This reduces upfront commitment while still covering peaks via burst (with throttle policy) but requires careful routing to maintain SLOs during sustained peaks.
- Option C (VPC/private subset): Reserve 24x GPUs for regulated-PII flows (private deployment) and 24x shared GPUs for non-PII; remaining peak handled by burst/on-demand.

Notes on latency:
- p95 is dominated by queueing under arrival bursts. If you keep utilization per GPU under ~60% of measured sustained capacity, p95 stays within target; that maps to provisioning ~2.5x the straight tokens/sec/GPU divider (hence our headroom factor).
- KV cache quality is important. Improving cache hit from 40% -> 55% reduces effective peak tokens by ~11% (material).

Open items for accurate costing:
- Confirm model choice (40B vs 70B) and quantization path. 70B would materially increase per-request compute and memory footprint.
- Provide a sample 48-hour request log (anonymized) to run through our simulator for a tighter recommendation.

If Saffron is comfortable, I can prepare an Option B commercial sketch (12x reserved + 60x burst) with expected monthly cost, cost per 1M tokens, and a two-month canary economics table.

Regards,

Summary of agreement points:
